title: Secretary of State of California

context.text: California uses a top-two primary: on June 2, 2026 Shirley Weber (D) received 55.7% and Don Wagner (R) 40.3%, ahead of two Green candidates, so the two advance to the general election.

candidates.name: Shirley Weber
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Shirley Weber is the incumbent Democratic Secretary of State. Her candidate statement says she was born in the Jim Crow South to sharecroppers, that 28 statewide and special elections have been held under her, and that she won court fights over voting rights.

background.text: Says she was born in the Jim Crow South to sharecroppers who could not vote and that her family later used its living room as a polling place in California.

priorities.text: Protecting voting rights: "I will never give up on protecting your voting rights."
Ensuring every eligible Californian can register and vote.

record.text: On September 14, 2026 issued a statement welcoming the U.S. Supreme Court's decision rejecting Postal Service restrictions on mail voting ahead of the general election.
On September 25, 2026 said California does not intend to use the federal SAVE database for voter eligibility checks following a Supreme Court ruling.
On October 15, 2026 released her office's response to a U.S. Department of Justice demand to review a list of individuals the federal government believes are likely noncitizens.

candidates.researchNotes: Her campaign site was not loaded; no direct statement on documentary proof of citizenship was found.

candidates.name: Don Wagner
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Donald P. (Don) Wagner is the Republican nominee. His candidate statement lists service as a member of the California Legislature, Mayor of Irvine and Orange County Supervisor, and as a business owner. He proposes requiring voter ID at the polls and returning mail ballots by Election Day.

background.text: Member of the California Legislature, Mayor of Irvine, Orange County Supervisor, and business owner, per his candidate statement.

priorities.text: Requiring voter ID at the polls.
Requiring mail ballots to be returned by Election Day.
Modernizing the Secretary of State's business-filing office to be business friendly.

candidates.researchNotes: Legislative votes were not researched. His statement supports voter ID at the polls; it does not address documentary proof of citizenship to register.
